decision: Keep a reproducible diagnostic compiler. Apply co-resident programs to adjacent model stages next; no model speedup or hardware-limit claim from this microbenchmark.

design.arithmetic: Existing BF16 or W8A16 projection/residual and FP32 LayerNorm kernels; no device arithmetic edits.
design.runtime: Two independent four-BO instruction streams selected after resolving both FIFO graphs. Byte-addressed runtime DMA with original typed static FIFOs. Both compilations must have byte-identical PDI before sharing xclbin and UUID. Session cache then shares one hardware context while preserving independent runs and instructions.
design.scope: Diagnostic roots only; production artifacts/runtime unchanged. Projection graph helper extraction reproduces both production BF16 and INT8 PDI and instruction files byte-for-byte.

protocol.order: Separate A1, shared B1, shared B2, separate A2 for each precision; serial C++ dispatch.
protocol.timing: Projection execute/wait wall time; excludes preceding norm call and all uploads/downloads/allocation/oracle work. Same-program means repeated projection; after_norm_program means alternating operations (one shared hardware program in arm B). Each case warms max(8,banks) calls.
protocol.validation: FP64 projection oracle for every bank; independent FP64 norm oracle; exact saved output comparisons after timing, immutable weights/input and guard checks. No tolerance changes.
protocol.precision_note: INT8 here is W8A16 with BF16 MAC; not evidence of native INT8 matrix arithmetic.

runtime_evidence.observation: xrt-smi reports exactly one active hardware context over eight columns, zero reported errors/migrations, during a separate shared INT8 probe. Query-instrumented timings excluded from A/B results.

validation.host: Release and test builds; 3/3 CTest passed.
validation.production_helper: Fresh BF16 and INT8 projection compilation compared byte-for-byte with production PDI and instructions; identical.
validation.hardware: All eight A/B/B/A benchmark trials passed; separate runtime-query trial passed.

interpretation: Shared-program alternation returns projection latency close to repeated-projection latency for both precisions across tested working sets.
This measures the benefit of co-resident programs plus shared context, not a decomposition of firmware load, scheduling, DMA or context-switch costs.
Full model placement, memory, numerical regression and whole-model A/B gates are still required. No hardware-limit conclusion.
next_action: Prototype co-resident norm/mix and attention projections while preserving independent DDR interfaces and submissions; verify stage outputs/guards, full model regression and whole-model timing.
